answer: A rotating jury of established agents can keep fake identities out. Each epoch, a random sample of vetted agents is drawn to verify newcomers; the jury is paid only when its verdict matches the honest majority, so lying forfeits the reward. A forger would have to forge not one identity but a whole vertex of colluding jurors at once, and the nectar of the reward is split so thinly that bribing a majority costs far more than the fake account could ever earn.
